correctness.rationale: An empty row or column forces both colors on every perpendicular line, so weight below 2m implies every line is nonempty. Let (a,b,c) and (p,q,r) denote the numbers of lines with palette {1}, {2}, {1,2} among rows and columns, respectively. With a,p positive, the ap crossings must carry color 1, and they cover none of the both-color lines, so the number of 1s is at least ap+max(c,r). The always valid color-1 line-cover bound is max(a+c,p+r); use the symmetric bounds for 2. With both monochromatic crossing products positive, use ap>=a+p-1 and bq>=b+q-1 to get at least m+n-2+|c-r|. With only one positive product, the ordinary line-cover bound for the other color gives at least m+n-1 (depending on which monochromatic row/column count vanishes). With no positive product, either all lines in one direction are both-colored or all rows contain one color and all columns the other. This establishes the lower bound. Two colors per row attain 2m. For n=m or m+1 and m<=3, the two corner-adjacent arms work: their shared missing corner sees one color along each direction, as does the remaining empty subboard. For m>=4, the two disjoint cyclic diagonals in the (m-2)-square give both palettes there; the monochromatic-only row/column intersections of matching colors are exactly the other selected cells. Their weight plus the square weight is m+n-2. A separate mask-based exact search through the candidate minimum for nine dimension pairs, including (4,5), reproduced the predicted values. Scope: both dimensions at least two, colored vertices exempt, disjoint one-color classes, neither set-valued nor proper rainbow domination. The graph-isomorphism and support partition ensure the same minimum for dual-server domination; the finite replay is corroboration, not the lower-bound proof.

evidence: Theorem 3.4 of Rao et al. characterizes only full selection by Delta(G)+Delta(H)<=1. Lange covers the same color model and supplies general regular-graph bounds, with Theorem 7 at k=r and weight |V|/2. Gravner et al. determine the ordinary 2-domination square value n via triangular Young domination.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The degree sum m+n-2>=2 only excludes full selection. Lange's induced-degree complement bound for regular graphs with k=2 is a 2-domination bound, and the exact k=r case applies here only to the 2-by-2 board. The ordinary square lower bound is n rather than 2n-2 in the nontrivial sizes.

evidence: K_m square K_n is the line graph of K_{m,n}; selecting edges red and blue so each unselected edge meets both color classes is exactly this rule. The definition in Rao et al. uses disjoint R and B and applies the neighbor requirement only outside their union.
